grid1ph.name: Single-phase supply
grid1ph.desc: Public low-voltage supply: line, neutral and, in TN-S, the protective conductor.

battery.name: Battery
battery.desc: Direct current source. It discharges when feeding loads and charges from solar panels.

solarPanel.name: Photovoltaic panel
solarPanel.desc: Converts sunlight into direct current. The current follows the irradiance.

transformer1ph.name: Single-phase transformer
transformer1ph.desc: Changes the voltage between two isolated circuits, for example 230/12 V for a bell.

mcb1p.name: Circuit breaker 1P
mcb1p.desc: Protects the cable against overloads and short circuits. It breaks a single pole.

mcb1pn.name: Circuit breaker 1P+N
mcb1pn.desc: Protects the line and also breaks the neutral. The most common breaker in homes.

fuseGG.name: Fuse gG
fuseGG.desc: Melts when the current is too high. After it blows it must be replaced.

rcd2p.name: Residual current device 2P
rcd2p.desc: Detects current leaking to earth and breaks the circuit. At 30 mA it protects people.

rcbo.name: RCBO
rcbo.desc: Combines a circuit breaker and an RCD: it protects the cable and people.

mainSwitch2p.name: Main switch 2P
mainSwitch2p.desc: Switches off the whole installation. It gives no overcurrent protection.

switch1.name: One-way switch
switch1.desc: Switches a load on and off. It must always break the line.

switch2p.name: Double-pole switch
switch2p.desc: Breaks line and neutral together, for example on a water heater.

stairSwitch.name: Two-way switch
stairSwitch.desc: Connects common C to terminal 1 or 2. Two of them control a lamp from two places.

intermediateSwitch.name: Intermediate switch
intermediateSwitch.desc: Goes between two two-way switches to control a lamp from three or more places.

pushButton.name: Push button
pushButton.desc: Closes its contact only while pressed. Used for bells and impulse relays.

impulseRelay.name: Impulse relay
impulseRelay.desc: Each pulse on the coil changes the contact state. Several buttons in parallel control the light.

lampIncandescent.name: Incandescent lamp
lampIncandescent.desc: A purely resistive load. Its brightness follows the power.

lampLed.name: LED lamp
lampLed.desc: Efficient lighting. Its driver keeps the brightness despite some voltage drop.

lampFluorescent.name: Fluorescent lamp
lampFluorescent.desc: Tube with an inductive ballast: low power factor, needs enough voltage to start.

socket.name: Socket outlet with earth
socket.desc: Outlet with line, neutral and earth. Choose the appliance and, for tests, a fault.

heater.name: Heater
heater.desc: High-power resistive load with a metal enclosure (class I).

bell.name: Bell
bell.desc: Sound signal, usually fed at 8–24 V through a transformer.

motor1ph.name: Single-phase motor
motor1ph.desc: Motor for pumps and compressors. At start-up it draws several times its rated current.

voltmeter.name: Voltmeter
voltmeter.desc: Measures the voltage between two points. Connect it in parallel.

ammeter.name: Ammeter
ammeter.desc: Measures the current flowing through it. Connect it in series.

energyMeter1ph.name: Single-phase energy meter
energyMeter1ph.desc: Measures voltage, current, powers and power factor, and adds up energy in kWh.

junction.name: Junction terminal
junction.desc: Joins several conductors at the same electrical point.

busbar.name: Busbar
busbar.desc: Distributes a line, the neutral or earth to several outputs.

earthElectrode.name: Earth electrode
earthElectrode.desc: Connects the installation to earth through resistance Ra. Required in the TT system.

shortCircuit.name: Short circuit
shortCircuit.desc: Connects two points with no resistance to test the protective devices.

earthFault.name: Earth fault
earthFault.desc: Simulates an insulation fault from a conductor to earth.

person.name: Person touching
person.desc: A person touches a point. Shows the current through the body and its effect.

frame.name: Board frame
frame.desc: Groups the devices of a board visually. It has no electrical effect.

note.name: Note
note.desc: Free text for instructions or remarks.

grid3ph.name: Three-phase supply
grid3ph.desc: 400/230 V supply with three phases and neutral, for motors and industrial boards.

mcb3p.name: 3-pole circuit breaker
mcb3p.desc: Protects the three phases of a three-phase circuit and cuts them together.

mcb4p.name: 4-pole circuit breaker
mcb4p.desc: Cuts the three phases and neutral, for three-phase circuits with single-phase loads.

motorBreaker.name: Motor circuit breaker
motorBreaker.desc: Protects the motor against short circuit and overload, with Ir set to the motor current.

thermalRelay.name: Thermal overload relay
thermalRelay.desc: Opens contact 95-96 when the motor draws too much current for too long.

phaseMonitor.name: Phase failure and sequence relay
phaseMonitor.desc: Closes contact 11-14 only with all three phases present and in the right order.

heater3ph.name: Three-phase heater
heater3ph.desc: Three heating elements in star, connected to the three phases.

capacitorBank.name: Capacitor bank
capacitorBank.desc: Supplies reactive power and improves the power factor of the installation.

powerAnalyzer.name: Power analyser
powerAnalyzer.desc: Measures voltage, current and power factor on each phase, and the total power.

phaseSequenceMeter.name: Phase rotation meter
phaseSequenceMeter.desc: Shows whether the phases are in direct or reverse order, or one is missing.

phaseLoss.name: Phase loss
phaseLoss.desc: Cuts one of the three phases to test what happens to the motor.

phaseReversal.name: Phase reversal
phaseReversal.desc: Swaps two phases: the motor turns the other way.

contactor3p.name: Contactor
contactor3p.desc: Coil-operated switch: the main contacts switch the motor and the auxiliaries 13-14 and 21-22 serve the control circuit.

auxRelay.name: Control relay
auxRelay.desc: Control relay with two NO and two NC contacts, without power contacts.

timerOn.name: On-delay timer
timerOn.desc: Switches contacts 15-16 and 15-18 a set time after the coil is energised.

timerOff.name: Off-delay timer
timerOff.desc: Keeps the contacts switched for a set time after the coil is de-energised.

buttonNO.name: NO push button (start)
buttonNO.desc: Green push button: closes contact 13-14 only while pressed.

buttonNC.name: NC push button (stop)
buttonNC.desc: Red push button: opens contact 11-12 while pressed.

emergencyStop.name: Emergency stop
emergencyStop.desc: Cuts the control circuit and stays latched until it is released.

selector012.name: 0-1-2 selector switch
selector012.desc: Three-position rotary switch: position 1 closes 13-14 and position 2 closes 23-24.

pilotLight.name: Pilot light
pilotLight.desc: Panel indicator lamp: running, tripped or power present.

limitSwitch.name: Limit switch
limitSwitch.desc: Contact operated mechanically when a part reaches the end of its travel.

floatSwitch.name: Float switch
floatSwitch.desc: Closes contact 13-14 at high level and 21-22 at low level.

pressureSwitch.name: Pressure switch
pressureSwitch.desc: Switches the contacts when the pressure passes the set value.

inductiveSensor.name: Inductive sensor
inductiveSensor.desc: Three-wire PNP sensor: detects metal without contact and puts 24 V on output BK.

photocell.name: Photoelectric sensor
photocell.desc: PNP sensor that switches output BK on when an object breaks the light beam.

motor3ph.name: Three-phase motor
motor3ph.desc: Induction motor for industrial machines; connected in star or delta on the terminal board.

starDeltaStarter.name: Star-delta starter
starDeltaStarter.desc: Starts the motor in star at one third of the current, then switches to delta by timer.

softStarter.name: Soft starter
softStarter.desc: Raises the motor voltage gradually during start-up, then bypasses itself.

vfd.name: Variable frequency drive
vfd.desc: Controls the motor speed through frequency, with acceleration and deceleration ramps.

plc.name: Programmable logic controller (PLC)
plc.desc: Reads 8 inputs at 24 V, runs a ladder program and drives 8 relay outputs.

meas.tripTime: Thermal trip time at this current

state.zone_AC3: AC-3: muscle contractions, hard to let go

event.control_unstable: The control circuit oscillates and does not settle
event.coil_burnt: The coil of {{device}} burnt out: it received {{voltage}} and is rated {{rated}}
event.contactor_no_hold: {{device}} dropped out when {{button}} was released: no self-hold
event.motor_phase_loss: A phase is missing at motor {{device}}
event.phase_fault: {{device}} detected a missing or reversed phase

source_short.title: Supply {{device}} is short-circuited
source_short.cause: Line and neutral of {{device}} are joined with no load between them.
source_short.hint: Remove the wire that joins line directly to neutral.
source_short.learn: A short circuit is a path with almost no resistance between line and neutral. The current rises to thousands of amperes and the protective device trips. There must always be a load between line and neutral.

load_no_return.title: {{device}} does not work
load_no_return.cause: Terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}} does not reach the neutral: the current cannot return.
load_no_return.hint: Connect terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}} to the neutral (blue wire).
load_no_return.learn: Current leaves the supply on the line, flows through the load and returns on the neutral. With no return path the circuit is open and no current flows.

terminal_unconnected.title: Terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}} is free
terminal_unconnected.cause: No wire is connected to terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}}.
terminal_unconnected.hint: Connect a wire to terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}}.
terminal_unconnected.learn: Every load needs two conductors: the line, which brings the current, and the neutral, which takes it back.

switch_on_neutral.title: Switch {{device}} is on the neutral
switch_on_neutral.cause: With {{device}} off, the load is still live: danger when changing the lamp.
switch_on_neutral.learn: A switch must break the line. If it breaks the neutral, the lamp goes out but the lampholder stays connected to the line and can give a shock.

pe_missing.title: The enclosure of {{device}} is not earthed
pe_missing.cause: In a fault, the enclosure of {{device}} becomes live.
pe_missing.hint: Connect the PE terminal of {{device}} to the earth bar (green-yellow).
pe_missing.learn: On a class I appliance, the earth carries the fault current away from people and makes the protective device operate.

cable_unprotected.title: The cable from {{from}} to {{to}} is not protected
cable_unprotected.cause: {{device}} is rated {{rated}} and the {{section}} cable only carries {{iz}}.
cable_unprotected.hint: Use {{nextSection}} cable or a {{lowerRating}} circuit breaker.
cable_unprotected.learn: The protective device is there to protect the cable. Its rated current must not exceed what the cable can carry (In ≤ Iz).

wire_color.title: Wrong colour on the cable from {{from}} to {{to}}
wire_color.cause: This conductor is $t(role.{{expected}}), but the cable is $t(color.{{actual}}).
wire_color.hint: Use a $t(color.{{expected}}) cable for this conductor.
wire_color.learn: Colours show what each conductor does: brown, black and grey for lines, blue for neutral, green-yellow only for earth.

mcb_magnetic_trip.title: Circuit breaker {{device}} tripped
mcb_magnetic_trip.cause: Short circuit: {{current}} flowed, {{ratio}} times its rated current.
mcb_magnetic_trip.hint: Find the line-to-neutral short and remove it before resetting.
mcb_magnetic_trip.learn: The magnetic trip is instantaneous. It acts when the current reaches several times the rated current, which only happens in a short circuit.

mcb_thermal_trip.title: Circuit breaker {{device}} tripped on overload
mcb_thermal_trip.cause: The connected appliances draw {{current}} and {{device}} is rated {{rated}}.
mcb_thermal_trip.hint: Split the loads over two circuits or reduce the power.
mcb_thermal_trip.learn: The thermal trip is slow. A bimetal strip heats with the current and trips when the overload lasts too long.

mcb_breaking_capacity.title: {{device}} cannot break this short circuit
mcb_breaking_capacity.cause: {{current}} flowed and the breaking capacity of {{device}} is {{icn}}.
mcb_breaking_capacity.hint: Choose a circuit breaker with a breaking capacity above {{current}}.
mcb_breaking_capacity.learn: The breaking capacity is the largest current the breaker can interrupt without being destroyed. It must exceed the short-circuit current at that point.

fuse_blown.title: Fuse {{device}} has blown
fuse_blown.hint: Remove the cause and replace fuse {{device}}.
fuse_blown.learn: A fuse has a calibrated wire that melts with the heat of the current. The higher the current, the faster it melts.

rcd_trip.title: RCD {{device}} tripped
rcd_trip.hint: Unplug the appliance at {{location}} and check its insulation.
rcd_trip.learn: The RCD compares the current going out on the line with the current coming back on the neutral. If some is missing, it is leaking to earth, maybe through a person.

wrong_voltage.title: {{device}} has failed
wrong_voltage.learn: Each appliance is made for one voltage. At twice the voltage, the power is four times higher and the appliance burns out.

voltage_drop.title: Voltage drop of {{drop}} at {{device}}
voltage_drop.cause: The {{section}} cable is {{length}} long; the limit is {{limit}}.
voltage_drop.hint: Increase the cable size or move the board closer.
voltage_drop.learn: Cables have resistance and use part of the voltage. The limit is 3 % for lighting and 5 % for other circuits.

cable_overload.title: The cable from {{from}} to {{to}} is overloaded
cable_overload.cause: {{current}} flows and the {{section}} cable only carries {{iz}}.
cable_overload.hint: Increase the cable size or reduce the load.
cable_overload.learn: An overloaded cable heats up and its insulation ages quickly. It can start a fire.

loose_connection.title: Loose connection on the cable from {{from}} to {{to}}
loose_connection.cause: The poorly tightened contact dissipates {{power}} and heats up.
loose_connection.hint: Tighten the connection of the cable from {{from}} to {{to}}.
loose_connection.learn: A loose connection has resistance. With current it heats up and can melt the terminal.

body_current.title: Dangerous current through {{device}}: {{current}}
body_current.cause: The enclosure of {{location}} is at {{voltage}} and nothing broke the circuit.
body_current.hint: Install a 30 mA RCD and connect the earth.
body_current.learn: Above 30 mA the current through the body can stop the heart. A 30 mA RCD and the earth connection break the circuit in time.

battery_empty.title: Battery {{device}} is empty
battery_empty.cause: The charge of {{device}} has reached zero.
battery_empty.learn: Autonomy is the capacity in Ah divided by the current. A bigger load drains the battery faster.

control_unstable.title: The control circuit oscillates
control_unstable.cause: {{device}} switches on and off endlessly: an NC contact feeds its own coil.
control_unstable.hint: Check the NC contacts of {{device}}, such as 21-22.
control_unstable.learn: If a relay contact switches off its own coil, the relay opens and closes forever. The control circuit never settles.

path_open.title: {{device}} does not work
path_open.cause: {{blocker}} is off and breaks the circuit.
path_open.hint: Switch {{blocker}} on with the Operate tool.
path_open.learn: Current only flows when the circuit is closed from the supply to the load, on both line and neutral.

load_no_supply.title: {{device}} does not work
load_no_supply.cause: Terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}} does not reach the line.
load_no_supply.hint: Connect terminal {{terminal}} of {{device}} to the line (brown wire).
load_no_supply.learn: The line brings current from the supply to the load. Without it, the load gets no voltage.

wire_cut.title: {{device}} does not work
wire_cut.cause: The cable from {{from}} to {{to}} is cut.
wire_cut.learn: A cut wire opens the circuit like a switch that is off, but you cannot see it. Measure with the multimeter: voltage on one side, nothing on the other.

source_off.title: {{device}} does not work
source_off.learn: Without a power source there is no voltage anywhere in the installation.

load_switched_off.title: {{device}} is switched off
load_switched_off.cause: The built-in switch of {{device}} is off.
load_switched_off.hint: Switch {{device}} on with the Operate tool.
load_switched_off.learn: Many appliances have their own switch or thermostat, which also cuts the current.

low_voltage.title: {{device}} gets too little voltage
low_voltage.hint: Check the supply and the voltage drops on the cables.
low_voltage.learn: Low voltage can come from a weak supply, long or thin cables, or loads in series.

load_ok.title: {{device}} is working
load_ok.cause: The circuit of {{device}} is closed and the voltage is enough.
load_ok.hint: Switch off a device upstream to see the effect.
load_ok.learn: A circuit works when there is a closed path from the line, through the load, to the neutral, with enough voltage.

not_a_load.title: {{device}} is not a load
not_a_load.cause: This check follows the path from a load to the supply.
not_a_load.hint: Choose a lamp, socket, motor or another load.
not_a_load.learn: Loads are the devices that use energy: lamps, sockets, heaters, motors.

coil_off.title: {{device}} does not work
coil_off.cause: The coil of {{blocker}} has no supply.
coil_off.hint: Press the start button or check why {{blocker}} does not pull in.
coil_off.learn: A contactor closes its contacts only when its coil is energised. Follow the control circuit up to the coil.

coil_voltage.title: The coil of {{device}} does not pull in
coil_voltage.hint: Replace the coil or supply the control circuit at {{rated}}.
coil_voltage.learn: The coil must receive its rated voltage. Below it, it does not pull in; far above it, it burns out.

load_phase_phase.title: {{device}} is connected between two phases
load_phase_phase.hint: Connect {{device}} between one phase and neutral.
load_phase_phase.learn: Between two phases there are 400 V; between a phase and neutral, 230 V. A 230 V appliance burns out at 400 V.

motor_no_hold.title: {{device}} stops when {{button}} is released
motor_no_hold.cause: No self-hold: contact {{contact}} of {{contactor}} is not in parallel with {{button}}.
motor_no_hold.hint: Connect {{contactor}}-{{a}} and {{contactor}}-{{b}} to the terminals of {{button}}.
motor_no_hold.learn: The start button closes only while it is pressed. The contactor NO contact, in parallel with the button, keeps the coil energised.

motor_overheated.title: Motor {{device}} burnt out
motor_overheated.cause: It ran too long above its rated current of {{rated}}.
motor_overheated.hint: Replace {{device}} and protect it with a thermal relay set to {{rated}}.
motor_overheated.learn: The thermal relay switches the motor off before the windings overheat. Without it, the insulation burns.

motor_overload.title: {{device}} tripped on overload
motor_overload.hint: Check the load on {{motor}} and reset {{device}} once it has cooled.
motor_overload.learn: Overload heats the motor slowly. The thermal relay copies that heating and opens the control circuit before the motor is damaged.

motor_phase_loss.title: A phase is missing at motor {{device}}
motor_phase_loss.learn: With two phases, a stopped motor has no torque to start. The current rises and the windings overheat.

motor_stalled.title: Motor {{device}} does not start
motor_stalled.cause: The rotor is locked or the {{load}} load is too high.
motor_stalled.hint: Free the rotor of {{device}} or reduce the load.
motor_stalled.learn: At standstill the motor draws 6 to 8 times its rated current. If it does not accelerate, it heats up in seconds.

overload_phase_loss.title: {{device}} tripped on phase loss
overload_phase_loss.cause: {{motor}} was left with two phases and drew {{current}}.
overload_phase_loss.hint: Check the three phases of {{motor}} before resetting {{device}}.
overload_phase_loss.learn: Without one phase, the other two carry too much current. The thermal relay senses the imbalance and trips faster.

vfd_undervoltage.title: Drive {{device}} stopped on undervoltage
vfd_undervoltage.cause: A phase is missing or the input voltage is low.
vfd_undervoltage.hint: Check the three input phases of {{device}} and reset the fault.
vfd_undervoltage.learn: The drive monitors its DC bus. Without enough voltage, it stops the motor to protect itself.

simpl.grid_ideal: Supply: ideal voltage source with a resistive impedance per conductor.
simpl.battery_linear: Battery: voltage linear with state of charge; no temperature or ageing effects.
simpl.solar_linear: Solar panel: source with internal resistance (no I-V curve or MPPT).
simpl.transformer_linear: Transformer: ideal, with 5 % resistive impedance and 2 % iron losses; no saturation.
simpl.mcb_thermal: Circuit breaker: thermal by I²t from 1.13 · In with t = 150 / ((I/In)² − 1.13²) s; magnetic at the upper limit of the curve.
simpl.fuse_table: gG fuse: indicative average IEC 60269 curve, interpolated; no manufacturing tolerances.
simpl.rcd_type: RCD: measures only the AC component; types AC and A behave the same.
simpl.lamp_resistance: Lamp: constant resistance (the real cold resistance is lower).
simpl.led_resistive: LED: modelled as a resistance; a real driver has almost constant power.
simpl.fluorescent_ballast: Fluorescent: fixed R + jX impedance; starts above 75 % of the voltage.
simpl.motor1_two_state: Single-phase motor: two states (starting and running) instead of continuous slip.
simpl.body_model: Human body: fixed 1000 Ω resistance; IEC 60479-1 zones approximated.
simpl.analyzer_fundamental: Power analyser: measures only the fundamental (50/60 Hz).
simpl.capacitor_ideal: Capacitor bank: ideal capacitors, without losses or automatic steps.
simpl.contactor_threshold: Contactor: pulls in at 75 % and drops out at 50 % of Uc, without closing time or bounce.
simpl.motor3_equivalent: Three-phase motor: equivalent circuit with R1 = R2, derived from the nameplate (In, PF and starting current).
simpl.motor3_sequence: Three-phase motor: torque from symmetrical components; the separate negative-sequence impedance is not modelled.
simpl.overload_thermal: Thermal relay: I²t heating above 1.12 · Ir and simple cooling, without ambient temperature.
simpl.plc_scan: PLC: the program runs at the simulator step (10 to 50 ms); 24 V DC inputs only.
simpl.pnp_sensor: PNP sensor: the output is a switch to positive, without voltage drop or delay.
simpl.soft_starter: Soft starter: voltage reduced by an ideal transformer, without thyristor harmonics.
simpl.star_delta_no_gap: Star-delta starter: switchover without dead time between star and delta.
simpl.vfd_vf: Drive: constant V/f model, without vector control; typical fixed input harmonics.

light-point.title: Simple light point
light-point.desc: Circuit breaker, switch on the line and one lamp. Switch S1 on with the Operate tool.

stair-light.title: Two-way lighting
stair-light.desc: Two two-way switches turn the same lamp on and off from two places.

house-board.title: Home distribution board
house-board.desc: Main switch, 30 mA RCD and three circuits: lighting, sockets and heating.

tt-protection.title: Protection of people in TT
tt-protection.desc: A faulty iron and a person touching it. Watch the RCD cut the leak, then switch it off to compare.

dol-start.title: Direct-on-line start with signalling
dol-start.desc: 4 kW motor with motor breaker, contactor, thermal relay, self-hold and running and trip pilot lights.

reversing.title: Reversing with interlock
reversing.desc: Two contactors swap two phases; contacts 21-22 stop both from closing at the same time.

star-delta.title: Star-delta start
star-delta.desc: 7.5 kW motor that starts in star and switches to delta after 5 s, with contactors and a timer.

vfd-motor.title: Motor with frequency drive
vfd-motor.desc: The selector drives the inverter through inputs DI1 and DI2: 5 s ramps in both directions.

plc-pump.title: PLC pump with float switch
plc-pump.desc: The PLC starts the pump when the float shows high level and lights the indicator; S0 stops it.

done.title: You built your first circuit!
done.text: You built, measured and protected a light point. The next step is the first exercise on the same topic.

light.title: My first light point
light.screen-canvas: This is the diagram: you build the circuit here, piece by piece.
light.screen-library: The library holds the devices. Drag them onto the diagram.
light.screen-props: Properties show the selected device, its settings and its measurements.
light.screen-sim: The simulation always runs. Here you can pause, step through and change the speed.
light.place-grid: Drag the Single-phase supply onto the diagram. It is the power source.
light.place-mcb: The circuit breaker protects the cable. Drag a 1P+N circuit breaker below the supply.
light.wire-phase: Connect the line: drag from terminal L of the supply to terminal 1 of the breaker. The wire turns brown.
light.wire-neutral: Now the neutral: from terminal N of the supply to the top N terminal of the breaker. The wire turns blue.
light.place-switch-lamp: Place a One-way switch and an Incandescent lamp to the right of the breaker.
light.phase-path: The line goes through the switch before the lamp. Connect breaker terminal 2 to the switch, and the switch to lamp terminal L.
light.neutral-return: Close the circuit through the neutral: connect the bottom N of the breaker to N of the lamp.
light.switch-on: Choose the Operate tool and click the switch to turn it on.
light.measure: Measure the voltage: choose the Probe and click terminals L and N of the lamp.
light.view-3d: Open the Physical 3D tab to see the real installation.
light.fault: Go back to the diagram. Place a Short circuit between L and N of the lamp and activate it with Operate.
light.fix: The breaker tripped. Click «How to fix» on the message, deactivate the short and reset the breaker.

motor.title: My first motor start
motor.intro: You will build a direct-on-line start for a three-phase motor. The power circuit goes on the left and the control circuit on the right.
motor.place-grid: Drag the Three-phase supply onto the diagram. It has three phases, L1, L2 and L3, plus neutral and earth.
motor.breaker: Place a Motor circuit breaker below the supply and connect L1, L2 and L3 to terminals 1, 3 and 5.
motor.contactor: The contactor switches the motor on and off. Place it below and connect breaker terminals 2, 4 and 6 to contactor 1, 3 and 5.
motor.motor: Place the Thermal relay and the Three-phase motor. Connect the contactor to the relay (2-1, 4-3, 6-5), the relay to the motor (U1, V1, W1) and earth to PE.
motor.control: Now the control circuit: from breaker terminal 2 to relay 95, then 96, stop button, start button and coil A1. Connect A2 to neutral.
motor.try-start: Choose Operate, press the start button and release it. Watch what happens to the motor.
motor.self-hold: The motor stopped when you released the button: there is no self-hold. Connect K1-13 and K1-14 to start button terminals 13 and 14 and start again.
motor.relay: Select the thermal relay and set Ir to the motor rated current, 7.7 A.
motor.phase-loss: Phase loss test: select the cable from relay 6 to motor W1 and tick «Cut wire».
motor.phase-fix: Read the message, click «How to fix» and reconnect the cut cable.
motor.done: You built a direct-on-line start with self-hold and a thermal relay, and saw how a phase loss is explained. Next comes the first industrial exercise.
